# 什么是知识面板（Knowledge Panel）？

- 原标题：What Is Knowledge Panel?
- 作者：Flavio Amiel Roborank 创始人
- 原文更新日期：2026-07-15
- 原文：https://roborank.io/glossary/knowledge-panel/
- 栏目：[AI Search & GEO](https://roborank.io/ai-search/)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。原文中的数据、观点、平台说明及推广内容均按原文保留，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

知识面板是 Google 为它在知识图谱中识别出的实体——人物、地点、组织或事物——展示的信息框。它会从网络各处的来源自动汇集名称、简介、图片和关键属性等事实，并在标准搜索结果旁边或上方提供一份便于快速查阅的摘要。

### 关键要点

- 知识面板是可见的展示形式；知识图谱是为它提供信息的底层事实数据库。
- Google 根据公开网络来源和授权数据合作伙伴的信息自动生成面板，你无法购买或直接创建它。
- 只有当 Google 从公开网络获得了足够多的实体信息，可以填充面板时，面板才会出现。
- 实体本人或官方代表可以通过身份验证认领面板，随后提出修改建议，但是否采用由 Google 审核决定。
- 拥有知识面板，说明该实体已进入知识图谱；但进入知识图谱，并不保证一定显示面板。

### 知识面板如何运作

知识面板从识别开始。Google 的文档将面板定义为：“当你搜索[知识图谱](https://roborank.io/glossary/knowledge-graph/)中的实体（人物、地点、组织、事物）时，在 Google 上出现的信息框。”因此，面板是先前判断的后续结果：Google 必须先识别一个现实世界中的[实体](https://roborank.io/glossary/entity/)，并确信自己了解它是什么，之后才会组装这个信息框。

组装过程是自动的。Google 表示，“知识面板是自动生成的，面板中显示的信息来自网络上的各种来源”，并由授权数据合作伙伴为体育、金融、天气等需要权威信息的主题补充资料。你不能提交一个面板，也不能付费购买。Google 会根据它已经找到并信任的内容，汇集名称、简短介绍、图片和关键属性。这也是为什么信息一致、描述清楚的[实体主页](https://roborank.io/glossary/entity-home/)，以及网络各处相互吻合的信号，才是决定面板是否会出现的真正影响因素。只有公开网络上存在足够信息可供填充时，面板才会显示。

对面板的管理通过认领实现，而不是直接编辑。如果你是实体本人或官方代表，可以验证身份并认领面板，随后提出修改建议。但建议不等于控制：Google 会审核每项修改提议，再决定是否采用。这与越来越多地影响 [AI 概览](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-overviews/)可见度的[实体优化](https://roborank.io/glossary/entity-optimization/)遵循同一种原则：把实体描述得足够清晰、一致，让 Google 的面板和生成式答案引擎都能毫不犹豫地识别并概括它。

### 知识面板示例

最基础、文档记录完整的例子，就是支撑所有知识面板的系统发布过程。**2012 年 5 月 16 日**，Google 发布[《推出知识图谱：关注事物，而不只是字符串》](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/introducing-knowledge-graph-things-not/)，宣布了知识面板背后的数据库。发布时，Google 表示，知识图谱“目前包含超过 5 亿个对象，以及超过 35 亿条关于这些对象的事实和对象之间的关系”。其初始信息来自 Freebase、Wikipedia 和 CIA World Factbook 等公开来源，之后又进行了更大规模的扩充。

这份公告最清楚地说明了面板究竟是什么，因为它明确了依赖关系。你看到的某个地标或公众人物的面板，并不是专门撰写的内容，而是 Google 读取其对象与事实数据库，再把这个实体最重要的事实呈现为一个框。Google 的帮助文档从另一个角度强化了这一点：当“公开网络上有足够多的信息”时，面板就会“由 Google 搜索算法自动创建”。那个包含 5 亿个对象的数据库是信息供给，面板则是 Google 展示其中某一个对象的方式。

这个教训可以直接用于策略。由于面板根据 Google 已经掌握并信任的事实生成，影响面板的方法与影响知识图谱本身相同：让实体身份毫不含糊，并让 Google 所查看的各处核心事实一致。在官方网站和权威资料页上使用相同名称、相同描述，以及可由机器读取的陈述；将这些陈述表达为清晰的[语义三元组](https://roborank.io/glossary/semantic-triple/)，即主体、关系、客体。正是这些重复出现的一致信息，让 Google 将实体从“网络上被提到的对象”提升为“已知且拥有面板的对象”。你无法亲手撰写面板，但可以提供证据，让 Google 有足够信心为你生成它，然后认领面板，保持细节准确。

### 人们容易弄错的一点

我经常看到团队试图“创建一个知识面板”，仿佛那是一张他们自己发布的网页。这做不到。Google 只有在确信实体存在、并对其掌握足够信息时，才会自动生成面板。你真正能控制的是证据：一致的名称、清晰的介绍，以及在 Google 已经信任的权威位置重复出现的相同事实。这些位置包括官方网站、维护良好的资料页，以及在各处用同样名称标识实体的结构化标记。当这些信号相互矛盾时，Google 会犹豫，面板就不会出现；当它们一致时，面板往往会自行出现。认领面板也重要，但这是面板已经存在*之后*才做的步骤，不能凭空变出一个面板。应把面板视为 Google 对实体理解程度的显示结果，而不是你能直接交付的一张页面。

### 知识面板与知识图谱的对比

|  | 知识面板 | 知识图谱 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **是什么** | 屏幕上显示某个实体的信息框 | Google 存储实体事实的数据库 |
| **作用** | 可见的展示界面 | 底层数据来源 |
| **范围** | 每个面板对应一个实体 | 覆盖所有实体的数十亿对象和事实 |
| **参与方式** | 认领并提出修改建议 | 提供一致、可信的事实供其吸收 |
| **存在条件** | 只有 Google 掌握足够信息时才显示 | 作为 Google 后台知识库一直存在 |

两者是一组“数据来源与展示形式”的关系，这也是它们容易被混淆的原因。知识图谱是数据库，存储关于人物、地点和事物的数十亿条事实；知识面板则是 Google 在结果页针对某个特定实体，展示该数据库一小部分内容的方式之一。有面板能确认实体已进入图谱，但很多实体即使存在于图谱中，也从未触发面板展示。

### 常见问题

#### 什么是 Google 知识面板？

它是 Google 为已识别实体自动生成的信息框，实体可以是人物、地点、组织或事物。面板会汇总来自网络各处的名称、描述、图片和关键属性等事实，并显示在常规搜索结果旁边。

#### 怎样获得知识面板？

你无法直接创建它。Google 识别某个实体，并在公开网络上获得足够多的一致信息后，会自动生成面板。完善官方网站、权威资料页，以及相互吻合的结构化数据，让 Google 能有把握地识别和描述实体。

#### 知识面板与知识图谱有什么区别？

知识图谱是 Google 存储数十亿条实体事实的数据库；知识面板是在屏幕上展示某个具体实体事实的信息框。图谱是来源，面板是利用这个来源的一种可见展示形式。

#### 可以编辑自己的知识面板吗？

你可以提出修改建议，不能直接修改。如果你是实体本人或官方代表，可以通过验证认领面板，然后提交修改提议。Google 会审核每项建议并决定是否采用，因此你拥有的是影响能力，而不是直接编辑权。

### 核心结论

知识面板是 Google 为其知识图谱中识别的对象，自行组装的实体摘要，包含名称、描述、图片和重要事实。它是理解的结果，而不是你创建的一张网页：当 Google 确信实体是谁或是什么时，面板就会出现，并从它在各处看到的一致、可信来源中获取内容。改善证据，面板往往也会随之出现；之后你可以认领它，进一步完善细节。

## 英文原文

A Knowledge Panel is the information box Google displays for an entity — a person, place, organization, or thing — that it recognizes in its Knowledge Graph. It automatically compiles facts such as a name, description, image, and key attributes from sources across the web, presenting a quick-reference summary beside or above the standard search results.

### Key Takeaways

- A knowledge panel is the visible display; the Knowledge Graph is the underlying database of facts that feeds it.
- Google generates panels automatically from sources across the open web and licensed data partners — you cannot buy or directly build one.
- A panel appears only when Google has enough information about an entity on the open web to populate it.
- The subject or an official representative can claim a panel through verification and then suggest changes, but Google reviews and decides what to apply.
- Having a knowledge panel confirms your entity is in the Knowledge Graph; being in the Graph does not guarantee a panel will appear.

### How Knowledge Panel Works

A Knowledge Panel starts with recognition. Google’s documentation defines panels as “information boxes that appear on Google when you search for entities (people, places, organizations, things) that are in the [Knowledge Graph](https://roborank.io/glossary/knowledge-graph/).” So the panel is downstream of a prior decision: Google must first identify a real-world [entity](https://roborank.io/glossary/entity/) and be confident it knows what that entity is. Only then does it assemble the box.

The assembly is automatic. Google states that “knowledge panels are automatically generated, and information that appears in a knowledge panel comes from various sources across the web,” supplemented by licensed data partners for authoritative topics like sports, finance, and weather. You do not submit a panel or pay for one. Google compiles the name, short description, image, and key attributes from what it already finds and trusts — which is why a consistent, well-described [entity home](https://roborank.io/glossary/entity-home/) and matching signals across the web are the real levers behind whether a panel appears at all. A panel shows up only when Google has enough information on the open web to populate it.

Ownership works through claiming, not editing. If you are the subject or an official representative of the entity, you can claim the panel by verifying your identity, after which you can suggest changes. But suggestion is not control: Google reviews each proposed edit and decides whether to apply it. This is the same [entity optimization](https://roborank.io/glossary/entity-optimization/) discipline that increasingly governs visibility in [AI Overviews](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-overviews/) — the goal is to make an entity so clearly and consistently described that both Google’s panel and generative answer engines can identify and summarize it without hesitation.

### Example of Knowledge Panel

The foundational, fully documented example is the launch of the system that powers every panel. On **May 16, 2012**, Google published [“Introducing the Knowledge Graph: things, not strings”](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/introducing-knowledge-graph-things-not/), announcing the database behind knowledge panels. At launch, Google stated the Knowledge Graph “currently contains more than 500 million objects, as well as more than 3.5 billion facts about and relationships between these different objects,” seeded from public sources including Freebase, Wikipedia, and the CIA World Factbook, then augmented at larger scale.

That announcement is the clearest illustration of what a panel actually is, because it makes the dependency explicit. The panel you see for, say, a landmark or a public figure is not authored content — it is Google reading its object-and-facts database and rendering the entity’s headline facts into a box. Google’s help documentation reinforces the point from the other direction: panels are “created automatically by Google Search algorithm when there is enough information available on the open web.” The 500-million-object database is the supply; the panel is one way Google surfaces a single object from it.

The lesson generalizes straight to strategy. Because the panel is generated from facts Google already holds and trusts, you influence it the way you influence the Graph itself: by making an entity’s identity unambiguous and its core facts consistent everywhere Google looks. The same name, the same description, and machine-readable statements — expressed as clean [semantic triples](https://roborank.io/glossary/semantic-triple/) of subject, relationship, and object — repeated across an official site and authoritative profiles are what let Google promote an entity from “mentioned on the web” to “known object with a panel.” You cannot write the panel, but you can supply the evidence that makes Google confident enough to write it for you, and then claim it to keep the details accurate.

### The thing people get wrong

The mistake I see constantly is teams trying to "build a knowledge panel" as if it were a page they publish. You can’t. Google generates the panel automatically once it is confident an entity exists and knows enough about it. What you actually control is the evidence: a consistent name, a clear description, and the same facts repeated across authoritative places Google already trusts — an official site, well-maintained profiles, and structured markup that names the entity the same way everywhere. When those signals conflict, Google hesitates and no panel appears. When they agree, the panel tends to show up on its own. Claiming a panel matters too, but it is a step you take *after* the panel exists — it does not conjure one into being. Treat the panel as a readout of how well Google understands your entity, not as a deliverable you can ship.

### Knowledge Panel vs Knowledge Graph

|  | Knowledge Panel | Knowledge Graph |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **What it is** | The on-screen box for one entity | Google’s database of facts about entities |
| **Role** | Visible display surface | Underlying data source |
| **Scope** | A single entity per panel | Billions of objects and facts across all entities |
| **You interact by** | Claiming it and suggesting edits | Supplying consistent, trusted facts to be ingested |
| **Existence** | Appears only when Google has enough info | Always present as Google’s backend knowledge base |

The two are a source-and-surface pair, which is why they get confused. The Knowledge Graph is the database — billions of facts about people, places, and things. A knowledge panel is one way Google renders a slice of that database for a specific entity on the results page. A panel confirms the entity is in the Graph, but plenty of entities sit in the Graph without ever triggering a panel.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is a Google Knowledge Panel?

It is an automatically generated information box Google shows for an entity it recognizes — a person, place, organization, or thing. It summarizes facts like a name, description, image, and key attributes, pulled from sources across the web, next to the regular search results.

#### How do I get a Knowledge Panel?

You cannot create one directly. Google generates a panel automatically once it recognizes an entity and has enough consistent information about it on the open web. Strengthen an official website, authoritative profiles, and matching structured data so Google can confidently identify and describe the entity.

#### What is the difference between a Knowledge Panel and the Knowledge Graph?

The Knowledge Graph is Google’s database of billions of facts about entities. A knowledge panel is the on-screen box that displays those facts for a specific entity. The Graph is the source; the panel is one visible surface that draws from it.

#### Can you edit your own Knowledge Panel?

You can suggest edits, not make them directly. If you are the subject or an official representative, you can claim the panel through verification and propose changes. Google reviews each suggestion and decides whether to apply it, so control is influence, not direct editing.

### The Bottom Line

A Knowledge Panel is the entity summary Google assembles on its own — a name, description, image, and headline facts — for something it recognizes in its Knowledge Graph. It is a symptom of understanding, not a page you build: it surfaces once Google is confident about who or what an entity is, and it draws its content from the same trusted, consistent sources everywhere Google looks. Improve the evidence and the panel tends to follow; you can then claim it to refine the details.
